text: child-page activities that need many short-lived visual elements use small DOM nodes with CSS keyframes and timer-based removal (ogrod.js) or a single canvas (akwarium.js); the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in style.css disables all animations, so removal must not depend on transitionend.
Reviewer check: compare the PR file list (gh pr view --json files) with what the description and index.html reference; a new activity JS file can be left untracked and missing from the commit.
When a reviewer reports a file missing from a PR, check git and disk first; it may never have been saved, so re-implement it from the PR description plus the existing CSS and HTML.
In this environment, run git as `git -C <dir>`; `cd <dir> && git ...` triggers an approval prompt and fails in unattended runs.
Reviewer check: Developer PRs can be stacked on unmerged sibling feature branches, so the diff against main includes other activities' files; note the merge order in the review.
child-page: the .n-lines SVG uses preserveAspectRatio=none; with vector-effect non-scaling-stroke removed, stroke widths and dasharrays in css/style.css are in viewBox (0-100) units, not pixels.
Reviewer check: activity buttons wired only to pointerdown with preventDefault() are not keyboard-activatable (Enter/Space fire click); note as a minor non-blocking suggestion.
Reviewer check: gh pr checkout can leave a stale detached HEAD from another branch; verify with `git fetch origin <branch>` and read files via `git show FETCH_HEAD:<path>`.

Reviewer check: for spring/physics-based motion, re-simulate the update step in Node (redirect mid-flight, landing time) to verify AC claims about continuity and duration instead of trusting the PR description.

Reviewer check: when a PR is re-labelled ready-for-review with an unchanged head sha, compare it with the previously reviewed sha first; if unchanged, post a short re-confirmation rather than a full re-review, and don't implement human-requested fixes yourself.

Reviewer check: in child-page akwarium.js the wall-avoidance margin must scale with turn radius (speed/turnRate), otherwise fish pin against walls on wide screens; margin ≈ 0.16·width is safe against overlap.

child-page: activity elements that must be keyboard-accessible need tabindex=0 plus a keydown handler for Enter/Space alongside pointerdown, and a :focus-visible outline in css/style.css; position dynamic nodes in percent so they survive orientation changes.
child-page: for keyboard activation of pointerdown-wired buttons, add a click listener guarded by e.detail === 0 (Enter/Space) and remove both listeners in the mount cleanup.

Reworker: the revisions-required label may show as 'revisions-required:wip' claim label; `gh pr edit --remove-label revisions-required` still works. child-page has no test suite, so verify JS with `node --check`.
child-page originally had no web app manifest, icons or service worker, so Chrome 'install' on Android only created a broken shortcut; installability/offline is tracked as a separate feature issue.

child-page: don't rely on SVG pathLength with stroke-dasharray for line-draw effects (unreliable across browsers); set the real length via a --len CSS variable computed in JS and use it for dasharray/dashoffset.

Reworker: `git merge` fails in this env without an identity; export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL (and GIT_AUTHOR_*) before merging main into a PR branch, then finish with `gh-as-agent commit` and `gh-as-agent push --repo <clone>` run from inside the clone dir.

child-page: the agent sandbox denies edits to .github/workflows/*; when a feature needs a pages.yml change (e.g. copying new top-level files into _site/), flag the exact change in a PR comment for a human instead of retrying.

child-page originally required 'no data stored'; features needing persistence (e.g. playtime timer) must explicitly relax that rule for minimal local-only storage and define a parent gate for any parent-facing Settings.

child-page: activities mount inside .stage, and the global `.stage svg {width:120px;height:120px}` rule (specificity 0,1,1) overrides single-class SVG sizing like .n-lines; scope activity SVG overlay selectors as `.stage .<class>` or they shrink to 120px and misalign with percent-positioned elements.
Reviewer check: when a child-page SVG overlay looks like a 'smaller separate shape', suspect the global `.stage svg` 120px rule and verify the overlay selector is scoped `.stage .<class>`.
child-page playtime limit design: timer counts only visible activity time, resets automatically each new day, and stores only the limit and time used locally (relaxing the 'no data stored' rule).

child-page: .github/workflows/pages.yml copies an explicit file list with `cp -r` into _site; if the workflow listing new paths (manifest.webmanifest, sw.js, icons) lands on main before the PR that adds them, the deploy job fails, so merge the feature PR first or together.

Reworker: an add/add conflict on a stacked PR's file means main already holds an older copy; keep the PR's newer version with `git checkout --ours <file>` during `git merge origin/main`, then re-check `gh pr view --json mergeable` after a few seconds because GitHub's status lags.

child-page: for SVG parts that must scale around a fixed point (e.g. butterfly wings folding to the body axis), set the SVG transform attribute (scale about user-space origin) from JS; CSS transform-box: view-box with transform-origin percentages ignores an offset viewBox (e.g. -50 -40 100 80) and folds toward the wrong side.

child-page: playtime limit lives in js/playtime.js (window.Playtime: start/stop/isExpired/renderLater) with state in localStorage key 'swa.playtime'; app.js only calls these, and dimming is set from JS (stage opacity) so it survives the global prefers-reduced-motion rule.

Reviewer check: child-page playtime.js re-reads state from localStorage every tick (refresh/load), so when storage throws the in-memory 'used' is discarded and the limit is never enforced; check storage-unavailable fallbacks in any reload-from-storage state code.

child-page playtime.js: when a localStorage write fails, keep an in-memory copy of state and have load() use it (storageOk flag) so refresh-from-storage doesn't discard used time; guard once-only expiry rendering with a per-start flag in app.js.
